answer: Dilution-weighted reputation curve. Each agent's influence equals reputation divided by the square of identities it controls, using a quill to sign one reputation ledger entry per identity per epoch. An attacker splitting into N identities pays N registration work plus ongoing ledger maintenance; marginal influence falls as 1/N. A copper fee per epoch entry funds review, and flagged clusters get routed to an oasis of isolated low-trust pools until manual clearance, so costs scale quadratically with cluster size.
